author: Independent education critic subagent (claude-opus-5-5); did not author the reviewed artifacts

findings.claim: The count rationale overstates why the count stops at 30. Section 7 says more items 'would repeat objectives rather than add coverage', and that the two untargeted objectives are tasks 'an MCQ cannot assess'. Section 4 (line 74) defines the primary objective as the one an item's result is reported against. Ten of the 40 claimed objectives are secondary only, so they shape context but are never reported: big-o#o1, choosing#o2, generics#o1, how-hashmap#o2, lists#o3, stacks#o3, equals#o2, grouping#o2, lambdas#o2 and streams-db#o1. Up to 10 more items, 40 in all and 80 minutes, inside the 45/90 cap, could make these primaries without repeating any primary, which would raise reported coverage. '30 = two per topic' is a design rule the plan chose, not a count that coverage forces. Also, an MCQ can partly assess collections-and-streams-review#o2 (for example, choosing the pipeline equivalent to a given loop). The coding practical's two tasks (equals/hashCode counting, then sort-and-group) do not ask for a loop-to-pipeline rewrite in either direction. Evidence: Programmatic check: primaries are 30 distinct objectives; set(secondaries) minus set(primaries) has 10 members, as listed above; Section 4 line 74: 'one primary objective, which is the objective its result is reported against'; collections-module-check blueprint instructions: Task 1 equals/hashCode plus merge/getOrDefault counting; Task 2 sort by two keys then group with a collector.
findings.recommendation: Restate the rationale honestly. Say 30 gives two reported items per taught topic and reports 30 objectives, with 10 more reached only as context. Name the alternative (up to 40 items/80 minutes to report all 40 objectives) and give the reason 30 better fits, or put that choice to the course owner. For collections-and-streams-review#o2, say it is better assessed by writing, not that an MCQ cannot assess it, and drop the claim that the practical assesses it unless a practical task actually does.

findings.claim: Section 6's differentiation list was not extended to cover the new items whose planned contexts restate existing topic-bank shapes. As written, these contexts are not clearly new or harder than the banks. q16 (drain a deque until the work runs out) matches stacks bank 'draining a queue in a loop' and 'element on an empty deque'. q17 (choose the safe replacement for a removal loop) matches lists bank 'removing while scanning' and 'relying on ConcurrentModificationException'. q18 (raw-type code hands data to generic code; where it fails) matches generics bank 'unchecked code fails later'. q24 (natural order with a missing entry) matches sorting bank 'nulls in the list' and the sorting page's nullsFirst(naturalOrder()) apply question. q26 (the one lambda that cannot become a method reference) matches method-references bank 'chained calls' and 'no existing method'. q28 (the collector that keeps every value for repeated keys) matches grouping bank 'o3 duplicate key' and 'o3 merge function', but only the scenario page is listed for q28. q09 (repair a captured variable) matches lambdas bank 'fix captured local'. The section 9 word-set similarity score (0.26) cannot detect reuse of the same structure under new wording. Evidence: Bank titles in collections-streams/collections-in-depth/{stacks-and-queues,lists-sets-and-maps-in-depth,generics,sorting-with-comparator}/artifact.gift and collections-streams/lambdas-and-streams/{method-references,grouping-with-streams-and-optional,lambdas-and-functional-interfaces-in-depth}/artifact.gift; collections-streams/collections-in-depth/sorting-with-comparator/artifact.md lines 110-114 (nullsFirst/nullsLast with naturalOrder apply questions); Section 6 lines 156-163 name none of these bank items for q09, q16, q17, q18, q24 or q26.
findings.recommendation: Add 'must not repeat' entries naming each of these bank items, and the sorting page's null apply question, for q09, q16, q17, q18, q24, q26 and q28. Have the private author check each authored item against them structurally (same mechanism plus same decision), not only by word overlap. Where an authored item matches, give it a second reasoning step or a cross-topic twist the bank lacks.

findings.claim: Two planned contexts appear to depend on mechanics the course does not teach, which contradicts line 72 ('Nothing needs material the course does not teach'). q17 asks learners to 'predict the result' of a removal loop that 'misses some'. The lists page and bank teach only that collection remove inside for-each can throw ConcurrentModificationException on a best-effort basis and can 'pass silently'. They never teach which elements an index-shifting or early-exiting loop skips, so predicting the exact survivors needs untaught List.remove index-shift or iterator internals. q19 ('a removal from a list of integer codes and a read into a primitive; predict the result') points at the List.remove(int index) versus remove(Object) overload. Neither the wrapper page nor the lists page shows that overload or List.remove(int). Evidence: collections-streams/collections-in-depth/lists-sets-and-maps-in-depth/artifact.md lines 32, 38, 68: only CME/best-effort, Iterator.remove and removeIf; lists bank feedback: 'Some removals finish without an exception and give a wrong result' (no mechanism taught); collections-streams/collections-in-depth/wrapper-types-and-autoboxing/artifact.md: no occurrence of 'remove'; coverage map line 84 (q19) and line 100 (q17).
findings.recommendation: Add section 8 rules. q17 must ask for the cause and the safe replacement, not the exact surviving elements, unless the course teaches index shift. q19 must not hinge on List.remove(int) versus remove(Object) overload resolution. Have the private author re-check the authored q17 and q19 against these rules. Alternatively, teach the mechanism on the relevant topic page in its own module branch before release.

findings.claim: q30 is now reported against collections-and-streams-review#o1, 'Retrieve, without notes, ...'. The blueprint's allowedResources (blueprint line 180) say the platform may allow 'notes, course pages or the Java API documentation'. If notes are allowed, a correct q30 does not show retrieval without notes, so reporting it against that objective is not valid. The context's own 'Without notes' cannot be enforced by an item. Evidence: authoring/catalog/collections-streams/lambdas-and-streams/collections-and-streams-review/topic.json o1 text; collections-streams/assessments/collections-streams-final-mcq/blueprint.json line 180.
findings.recommendation: Make q30's primary an objective whose condition the MCQ can meet, such as how-hashmap-works#o1 or the-equals-and-hashcode-contract#o1, and keep review#o1 as secondary or untargeted with a reason. Otherwise record that the final runs closed-book and that the platform owner must confirm it. Keep the blueprint objectives and the section 5 tables consistent.

findings.claim: '40 of the 42 course objectives' (also line 168 and section 9 line 188) miscounts the course. The catalog holds 45 objectives, because course-review/collections-and-streams-review-scenarios/topic.json defines o1-o3. The 42 counts the taught-topic objectives only. Line 136 explains why the scenario page has no item of its own, but the plan never accounts for its three objectives. Evidence: Programmatic count over authoring/catalog/collections-streams/**/topic.json: 45 objectives; untargeted = review-scenarios#o1,#o2,#o3 plus timed#o2 and review#o2.
findings.recommendation: Say '40 of the 42 taught-topic objectives'. Add one line saying the scenario page's three objectives restate taught objectives and are reached through q13/q23 (structure choice), q05/q14 (grouped and Optional results) and q28 (repeated-key collector), or list them as untargeted with that reason.

findings.claim: The envelope section is honest that the 60-minute MCQ plus the 30-minute practical need 90 minutes, 45 more than the module-check block. It does not say the F28 day is already fully allocated (15+20+25+45+15 = 120), so the day would run 165 of 120 minutes unless something moves. Line 170 ('Topic budgets stay inside it ... (gate T14)') could be read as saying the day fits. The unresolved placement is also missing from section 9's 'Not yet done' list, so nothing marks it as a release dependency. Evidence: coverage map lines 170-171 and 189.
findings.recommendation: State that F28 would total 165 of 120 minutes as planned. Make clear that the T14 pass covers topic budgets only, not assessment time. List the extra 45 minutes as an open course-owner decision in section 9 next to the JDK 25 re-run and the pilot timing.

findings.claim: q29's 'planned context' ('State the time complexity of a short interview solution out loud') copies the objective text; it is not an applied context. 'Out loud' has no meaning in an MCQ. Its objective pair (timed#o3 and #o1) is the mirror of q15's (#o1 and #o3), and q15's context is 'match a problem to its pattern and state the cost'. As planned, the two items test nearly the same task, one at Apply and one at Evaluate, with nothing to separate them. Evidence: coverage map lines 89 and 110; authoring/catalog/collections-streams/lambdas-and-streams/timed-coding-screen-patterns/topic.json o3 text.
findings.recommendation: Give q29 a concrete value-free context that differs from q15. For example, q29 traces the cost of a given short solution built on a structure q15 does not use, while q15 chooses between two candidate approaches under a stated input size. Drop 'out loud'.
